title: UniverLab audit document, v1
description: Versioned contract for a UniverLab audit page: metadata, findings, assets, deliverables and sections of typed blocks. A document declares contract 'univerlab.audit/1'. Unknown block types and properties prefixed 'x-' are valid extension points; renderers skip unknown blocks and validators warn about them. Breaking changes require 'univerlab.audit/2'.

contract.description: Contract version this document is written against. Must be exactly 'univerlab.audit/1' for v1 documents.

meta.description: Descriptive metadata: title, language, client, auditors, audit period, version, status and scope.

visibility.description: Whether the audit page is public or restricted. Private audits list reader emails in 'access'; the access list is contract data only and is never sent to the browser.

access.description: Reader allowlist for private audits: the email addresses allowed to read it. Required and non-empty when visibility is private; ignored for public audits. Never sent to the browser.

accent.description: Optional accent from the site palette tinting the audit page. Omitted means the renderer default. Part of how two audits look different without new code.

badge.description: Optional badge for a published audit: issue date, validity, a short scope line and an optional link to the previous audit of the same system. Old documents without it stay valid.

cover.description: The audit cover, which also picks a layout like any section.

assets.description: Asset catalogue: every file the document references, each with an id, a path inside the audit folder, a kind, a title, alt text where it applies, and its size and SHA-256 so the validator can confirm the file. Annex files are catalogue assets too, referenced by id from the annex.

annexes.description: Optional annexes: described deliverables with instructions, each bundling one or more catalogue asset files and carrying its own visibility. Private annexes stay off the public page and its files answer 404 on the public route.

deliverables.description: Downloadable deliverables by asset id. The page never generates a PDF itself; the TeXForge PDF report is required once status is delivered or final.

findings.description: Ranked findings, each with severity, likelihood and impact, area, status, evidence, recommendation, effort, optional cost and the version where it was fixed.

sources.description: Sources cited by prose, quotes and evidence entries.

glossary.description: Glossary terms that prose can reference inline for interactive definitions.

sections.description: Ordered page sections. Each picks a layout and holds an ordered list of blocks; two audits look different through different layouts, accents and block orders, not new code.

^x-.description: Extension point: properties prefixed 'x-' carry tool-specific data and are always valid.

version.description: Document version, e.g. '1.0'. Findings fixed later name the version that fixed them.

status.description: Lifecycle status. Delivered and final audits must name their TeXForge PDF report in deliverables.

scope.description: What the audit covers and, briefly, what it leaves out.

asset.title: Asset
asset.description: One file in the audit folder catalogue, verified by the validator against the file on disk.

id.description: Unique asset id used by blocks, evidence, deliverables and annexes to reference this file.

path.description: File path relative to the audit folder, e.g. 'assets/report.pdf'.

kind.description: Asset kind. Conveniences the renderer knows: pdf, image, video, audio, data, code, archive. Media kinds (image, video, audio) require alt text. Any other non-empty kind is valid: the page shows it by file extension and media type.

title.description: Human-readable asset title for download cards and captions.

alt.description: Alt text for media assets (image, video, audio). Required by the validator for those kinds.

bytes.description: Exact file size in bytes; the validator compares it against the file on disk.

sha256.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the file; the validator recomputes it from disk.

instructions.description: Optional usage instructions as Markdown without raw HTML, e.g. how to run a sandbox.
